lines.trans: We have not told them yet that the stage floor is glass, right?
Wow, in five years of doing Music Bank I barely exchanged a word with them—you are something else.
Are you working at a broadcasting station just to make friends with celebrities?
Every single meeting, whenever I ask you to come up with an idea…
you sit there with your lips clamped shut staring only at your phone!
And what on earth is that outfit—are you an idol?
Aw, come on—it is just because our youngest writer is so sociable.
That is a really great strength for a broadcast writer.
Oh, sure, right!
What a truly tremendous strength that is, right?

meanings.note: refers to something known to both speakers or near the listener

examples.trans: That movie was really fun.
What is that person's name?

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.

meanings.note: Compound of 하다 (to do) and 주다 (to give).

examples.trans: Please help me (do helping for me).
Please do this for me.

examples.trans: Wow, in five years of doing Music Bank I barely exchanged a word with them—you are something else.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

meanings.note: Combines with 하다 in 말하다 (to speak, to say).

examples.trans: I don't know what you mean.
You speak Korean well.

meanings.note: Placed before a verb to express inability or impossibility.

examples.text: 어제는 너무 피곤해서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.trans: I was so tired yesterday that I couldn't sleep.
Because it rained, we couldn't go on the picnic.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.trans: Wow, in five years of doing Music Bank I barely exchanged a word with them—you are something else.

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, younger people, or children

examples.trans: Wow, in five years of doing Music Bank I barely exchanged a word with them—you are something else.

meanings.note: Placed directly before a noun in questions

examples.trans: What kind of music are you listening to right now?
Is something the matter?
Did you hear about this celebrity?
I was busy today because of celebrity.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 너 무슨 연예인하고 친해지려고 방송국 다니는 거니?
examples.trans: Are you working at a broadcasting station just to make friends with celebrities?
This expression comes from 'in order to get close'.

meanings.note: 방송 (broadcasting) + 국 (bureau/station)

examples.trans: I have to go to the TV station this afternoon.
Fans are waiting in front of the broadcasting station.

meanings.en: to go around, to attend, to commute
meanings.note: Indicates regular movement or carrying something around constantly.

examples.trans: I commute to the company.
I carry a bag around with me.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.en: always, all the time, every day
meanings.note: colloquial pronunciation/variant of 만날; often carries mild exasperation

examples.trans: He always comes late.
Why do you make the same mistake every time?

meanings.note: Sino-Korean noun; 회의를 하다 means 'to hold a meeting'.

examples.trans: There is a meeting at four in the afternoon.
Please prepare the meeting materials in advance.

meanings.note: Available time or duration.
Used with native Korean numbers to count hours (한 시간 = one hour).

examples.trans: Do you have time?
It takes two hours.

examples.text: 아, 정말요? 와, 아이디어 진짜 좋다.
examples.trans: Oh, really? Wow, what a truly great idea.
The topic of idea came up during this shoot.
Please give me some water.
Please wait just a moment.

meanings.note: Contraction of 조금

examples.text: 지는 티 안 내려고 무지 애쓰는데 원래 티가 나는 거예요.
examples.trans: He tries hard not to let it show, but feelings like that always show.

examples.text: 티 안 내려고 무지 애는 쓰시는데 저는 조금 알 것 같습니다.
examples.trans: She tries hard not to show it, yet I think I understand that feeling a little.

examples.trans: Who said that?

examples.trans: Open mouth.
Mouth hurts.

examples.trans: you sit there with your lips clamped shut staring only at your phone!

meanings.note: Action of taking a seat.

examples.trans: Please sit on the chair.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)
meanings.note: Opposite of 없다.
Marks the possessed item with 이/가.

examples.trans: Do you have time?
Nobody is at home.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.note: Contraction of 아이.
Colloquially used to refer to people of the same age or younger.

examples.trans: Kids are running around and playing in the park.
That person has a really good personality.
I bought bread. And I bought milk too.
Let's eat and then depart.
The outfit you're wearing today is really pretty.
It's cold, so please wear warm clothes.

meanings.note: Demonstrative pronoun referring to something near the listener or already mentioned. Routinely spoken as 그거. RR: geugeot; spoken geugeo.

examples.trans: That is my mobile phone.
That is really important.

meanings.note: colloquial contraction of 무엇; also used rhetorically to brush off a question

examples.trans: What are you doing now?
Why are you even asking something like that?
Did you hear about this idol?
I was busy today because of idol.
Aw, really!
Oh, what a surprise.

meanings.en: older sister; older female friend or senior
meanings.note: Used by a younger male speaker.

examples.trans: I have one older sister.
Nuna, do you have time today?

meanings.note: 1st person plural pronoun; also used for 'my' with family, school, or workplace

examples.trans: Our team has a good atmosphere.

examples.text: 원래 연예인 하려다 작가 되신 거 아니에요?

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

meanings.note: Used when repeating an action.

examples.trans: See you again!

좋다.gloss: to be good, to be nice

examples.trans: I feel really good today.

그렇다.gloss: to be so, to do so

meanings.note: ㅎ-irregular; also used as a pro-verb ('do so / say so')

examples.trans: Is that really so?
Don't keep acting like that.

examples.trans: They say CEO Byun and Joon-mo traded harsh words and the set turned into a total mess.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).
